prompt:
solution.py is meant to implement the specification below, but it contains several defects. One has been reported: `satisfies("0.3.0", "^0.2.3")` returns True instead of False. Fix that and every other deviation from the specification. Keep the public names and signatures unchanged and do not change behaviour the specification requires.

Specification: Implement `satisfies(version, spec)` in solution.py and return a bool. A version is `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`: three non-negative integers without leading zeros (a lone 0 is fine). A spec is one or more alternatives separated by `||`; the version satisfies the spec if it satisfies any alternative. An alternative is one or more comparators separated by whitespace, all of which must hold. Comparators: a bare version or `=version` (equal); `>`, `>=`, `<`, `<=` followed directly by a version; `^version` (at least that version and below the next version that increments its left-most non-zero component: ^1.2.3 is below 2.0.0, ^0.2.3 is below 0.3.0, ^0.0.3 is below 0.0.4, and ^0.0.0 is below 0.0.1); `~version` (at least that version and below the next minor version: ~1.2.3 is below 1.3.0); and `*`, which any version satisfies. Inside a comparator the version may leave out trailing components, which count as zero before any rule is applied (`>=1.2` means `>=1.2.0`, `^1` means `^1.0.0`). The `version` argument itself must have all three components. Raise ValueError for a malformed version or spec: an empty spec or empty alternative, an unknown operator, whitespace between an operator and its version, leading zeros, more than three components, or non-digit components. A malformed spec raises even when another alternative already matches.
acceptance: caret follows the left-most non-zero component
tilde stays within the minor version
